lesson_title: Your Kitchen Is a Chemistry Lab
hook_text: Your kitchen has acids, bases and neutrals hiding in plain sight. Some are snacks. Some can burn you.
clip_script: The sour team: acids. Lemon juice has citric acid, vinegar has acetic acid, amasi has lactic acid. Cooldrinks are acidic too, which is why sipping them all day wears down your teeth. Acids turn blue litmus paper red. The soapy team: bases. Baking soda, toothpaste, soap. They feel slippery and turn red litmus blue. Now the dangerous ones: battery acid on one side, drain cleaner on the other. Both can burn skin and eyes. In the middle: neutral stuff like pure water and sugar water, which leave litmus alone. And when acid meets base, they cancel out into salt and water. That is why an antacid fixes heartburn, and why farmers spread lime on sour soil.
visual_style: Whiteboard kitchen with items lighting up red for acid, blue for base, green for neutral; litmus strips flipping colour; a handshake animation for neutralisation.
mood: Curious kitchen tour with a safety edge.
pacing: Quick sorting of foods, a sharp danger warning, a satisfying neutralisation finish.
